cards.text: Nehemiah, the man rebuilding Jerusalem's wall, is telling this one himself. His enemies Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab and the rest hear that the wall is rebuilt, with not one gap left. The doors aren't hung in the gates yet, but friend, that wall is UP.

cards.question: Sanballat and Geshem send Nehemiah a message. Where do they want to meet him?

answers.text: In a village on the plain of Ono
In the royal palace at Susa

cards.question: Sanballat and Geshem have no plans to harm Nehemiah.

cards.text: Nehemiah doesn't go. He sends messengers back with an answer instead.

cards.question: What reason does Nehemiah give Sanballat and Geshem for not coming to the meeting?

answers.text: He's doing a great work and can't stop
He's too sick to make the long trip
He's waiting for orders from the king

cards.text: They send the same message FOUR times, friend. I've had oven timers give up sooner than these guys.

cards.question: Four times the same invite comes, and each time Nehemiah sends back the ___ reply.

cards.text: The fifth time, Sanballat sends the same message with his young servant. And this time the servant has a letter in his hand.

cards.question: The letter Sanballat's servant carries is sealed.

cards.text: The letter says it's reported among the nations that Nehemiah and the Jews are up to something, and Geshem agrees. GESHEM, friend, the same guy who's been sending the invites!

cards.question: Sanballat's letter claims the Jews are building the wall for a reason. What is it?
Sanballat's letter says that, according to these reports, Nehemiah is going to become their ___.

cards.text: The letter even says he's appointed prophets in Jerusalem to proclaim, 'There is a king in Judah.' Then it warns that soon these rumors will reach the king, so come on, let's talk.

cards.question: Nehemiah writes back to Sanballat. Where does he say these rumors really came from?
Nehemiah says that with all these messages, his enemies are trying to frighten the Jews.
Nehemiah's enemies say the Jews' hands will be weakened in the work. What does Nehemiah pray?

answers.text: That God would strengthen his hands
That God would weaken their hands
That God would scatter his enemies

cards.text: Later, Nehemiah goes to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, a man who is confined to his house.
Shemaiah warns that they're coming to kill Nehemiah by night, and he wants to meet. Friend, everybody in this chapter wants a MEETING!

cards.question: Shemaiah wants Nehemiah to meet him inside the ___ and shut the doors behind them.
Nehemiah agrees to hide in the temple to save his life.

cards.text: Nehemiah says, "Should a man like me run away?" Friend, a stamper like me would already be in that temple with the doors shut and a chair shoved against them.

cards.question: Nehemiah realizes God didn't send Shemaiah. So why did Shemaiah give that prophecy?

cards.text: So that scary warning was bought and paid for. Shemaiah was hired to intimidate Nehemiah into doing what he suggested.

cards.question: If Nehemiah had hidden in the temple, what did his enemies hope would come of it?

answers.text: He would sin and get a bad name
He would be trapped and arrested
He would give away the city's plans

cards.text: Nehemiah hands it over to God. He asks God to remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they've done, along with Noadiah the prophetess and the other prophets who tried to intimidate him.

cards.question: Through every plot, the work goes on. The wall is completed in ___ days, on the twenty-fifth of Elul.

cards.text: FIFTY-TWO DAYS for a whole city wall! Friend, if folks were sending me scary letters all day, I wouldn't finish ONE cookie box in fifty-two days.

cards.question: When the enemies hear the wall is done, all the surrounding nations are ___ and ___.
Why does the finished wall leave the surrounding nations feeling that way?

answers.text: They hear the king approves it

cards.text: Meanwhile, back in Judah, the mail is BUSY. The nobles of Judah send Tobiah many letters, and Tobiah's letters keep coming back to them.

cards.question: Many in Judah are bound by oath to Tobiah because of family ties through marriage.

cards.text: Tobiah is the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah. And his son Jehohanan married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.

cards.question: The nobles of Judah keep telling Nehemiah about Tobiah's good deeds.
The nobles pass Nehemiah's words along to Tobiah. And what does Tobiah keep sending Nehemiah?

answers.text: Workers to help on the wall

cards.text: The wall is up, but Tobiah's letters keep coming. Hold that thought, friend, because Nehemiah has plenty more ahead of him.

findings.problem: The question says Nehemiah 'writes back' to Sanballat. Nehemiah 6:8 says only 'I sent him this reply.' Earlier in the passage his replies went by messengers (6:3), and the text never says this one was written.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This card asks what the enemies hoped would happen if Nehemiah hid in the temple. The right answer is 'He would sin and get a bad name.' No earlier card says that going into the temple to save his life would be wrong. Card 5 quotes only 'Should a man like me run away?' and leaves out 'Should one like me go into the temple to save his own life?' (6:11). Without that line, the baker has nothing to rule out 'He would be trapped and arrested.'

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This two-blank card ('all the surrounding nations are ___ and ___') sets 'afraid' as blank 1 and 'disheartened' as blank 2. Either order makes sense, so a baker who picks 'disheartened' then 'afraid' could fairly argue they got it right but would be marked wrong. The no-near-matches rule only covers wrong answers. No rule covers two right answers that can swap places.
findings.question: When the two blanks of a fill-in-the-blank card can swap places, should the card be rewritten so the order is clear, or should either order count as right?

findings.problem: The question asks 'Why does the finished wall leave the surrounding nations feeling that way?' The words 'that way' point back to card 12, which is no longer on screen. The question should say the feeling, for example 'afraid and disheartened.'

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'The wall is up, but Tobiah's letters keep coming,' only repeats what cards 10 and 18 already covered and doesn't move the passage forward. Card 18 already asked about 6:19, the passage's last verse, so this card can be just the story-isn't-over line.
